title: 🌿 The Cypress Throne
description: A historical fantasy of court intrigue, frontier pressure, and an ancient covenant in the mourning city of Selucor

nodes.label: Black Sails
text: Black funeral sails hang over Selucor as your ferry glides beneath the palace hill and its cypress terraces. 🌿
You have not seen the capital since exile, but the bronze domes and sea walls remember you too well.

nodes.label: First Step
text: Pages wait at the dock, bells sound from the shrine stair 🕯️, and cavalry banners flash at the upper gate.
Before the regent's summons catches you, you can enter Selucor by memory, trade, or prayer.

nodes.label: Palace Gate
text: At the upper gate, Captain Soren Vale reins in beside you with rain on his cloak and surprise in his eyes.
He does not waste words on welcome, but relief crosses his face before discipline buries it.

nodes.label: Harbor Road
text: The harbor road smells of tar, wet rope, and quince from the river barges crowding the lower quay.
Lady Danira Sol looks up from a grain scale and mutters that the Kardeshi envoy arrived under too many guards.

nodes.label: Shrine Stair
text: Mother Calia waits beneath the hill cypresses as though the stones warned her you were coming.
She touches your sleeve once and says, "Old words are waking, child of ink."

nodes.label: Regent Summons
text: Regent Iria Valen receives you in a chamber still draped for mourning, maps and sealed ledgers spread around her like weapons.
A piece of the Covenant of Bridges is missing 📜, the boy prince must be crowned, and a peace embassy from Kardesh is already inside the city.

nodes.label: Ready Service
text: You bow and take the charge before caution can intervene.
Iria's shoulders ease by a fraction, which is how she shows gratitude when the court can see her.

nodes.label: Hard Terms
text: You ask what price follows obedience this time. Iria answers without flinching: "Truth, if we can still afford it."
The candor unsettles you more than a lie would have.

nodes.label: Old Exile
text: You remind her that Selucor once sent you away in disgrace beside your father's name.
Iria accepts the wound without argument and says only, "Then help me stop this city from earning another."

nodes.label: Court Tide
text: Before more can be said, pages, harbor officers, and shrine novices collide around you in a tide of urgent messages.
Mourning has not slowed the court; it has only sharpened every errand.

nodes.label: Dust Archive
text: A page hustles you from Iria's chamber to the state archive, where cedar dust and old lamp oil hang over a bronze-bound chest left open on the table. 📚
One seal has been cut too neatly to be honest; whoever touched it knew court habits better than any common thief.

nodes.label: Young Prince
text: Another summons sends you to Prince Alexen's schoolroom, where river maps and toy soldiers are arranged like real provinces.
He asks whether old books can stop men from killing each other, and you cannot answer quickly.

nodes.label: Salt Jetty
text: Down at the salt jetty, the Kardeshi envoy Tamar Kesri steps ashore in dark riding silk, composed enough to make the whole harbor look theatrical.
When Tamar learns your name, the envoy's expression suggests Kardesh keeps better records than Selucor admits.

nodes.label: First Duty
text: After the first rush of messages, Iria wants movement before rumor hardens into certainty.
You can inspect the broken archive chest, go greet the Kardeshi envoy Tamar Kesri, or walk the painted gallery where the founders hid their history in plain sight.

nodes.label: Broken Chest
text: Inside the chest, tax tablets remain neatly stacked, but one folded parchment case is missing from the center.
The dust suggests it was removed recently and by patient hands.

nodes.label: Envoy Court
text: Tamar receives you in a wind-bright harbor court, with Kardeshi guards pretending not to watch every roofline.
The envoy says peace remains possible, but not if Selucor arrives at ceremony empty-handed and proud.

nodes.label: Painted Gallery
text: The imperial gallery carries painted bridges, cypress groves, and long-dead rulers clasping hands with riders from the eastern plain.
One damaged panel shows a treaty scene scratched almost blank around the witnesses.

nodes.label: First Inquiry
text: Three questions rise above the rest: what was taken, who profits from the raids, and what the dead emperor was trying to say before fever closed his mouth.
The answer you chase first will color everything after.

nodes.label: Missing Leaves
text: The missing case held the final leaves of the Covenant of Bridges, copied twice and sealed under imperial bronze.
Without them, no one can prove the exact obligations owed to Kardesh or the river cities.

nodes.label: Border Smoke
text: Reports show recent raids striking grain roads and ferries rather than frontier forts, which is a merchant's pattern, not a conqueror's.
Someone wants hunger and blame more than territory.

nodes.label: Last Words
text: A palace physician tells you the emperor woke only once on his final night and said, "The bridges remember before crowns. 👑"
The phrase sounds less like delirium than a warning he died too late to explain.

nodes.label: Sunset Pull
text: As evening bells answer harbor horns, the streets choke with mourners, traders, and torchbearers bound for competing duties.
Selucor decides whether you reach the regent's lamps, the wharves, the shrine, or lose precious time in the painted gallery again.

nodes.label: Supper Lamps
text: In a supper chamber lit by mourning lamps, Iria eats almost nothing and listens to everyone as if measuring knives by weight.
She asks which danger feels closest: the court, the harbor, or the memory under the hill.

nodes.label: Wharf Alarm
text: At the western wharves, a grain lock has been cut and guards are shouting over one another while sacks burst underfoot.
Danira swears the theft is too clumsy to be ordinary smuggling.

nodes.label: Cypress Vespers
text: Beneath the palace hill, shrine bells tremble through cypress smoke and old stone as Calia begins evening prayers.
When she names the founders, a draft moves through the chamber with no open door to blame.

nodes.label: First Trust
text: By nightfall, Selucor offers three possible centers of gravity and none of them are safe.
You can lean toward Iria's statecraft, Soren's frontier instincts, or Calia's older understanding of the city.

nodes.label: Regent Quiet
text: Iria speaks plainly once the chamber empties. She fears not foreign invasion but domestic men who profit whenever the border burns.
It is the kind of honesty rulers seldom survive for long.

nodes.label: Soldier Walk
text: Soren walks you along the wall circuit where the harbor lights look like embers on black cloth.
He says the riders on the frontier are angry, tired, and one bad week away from wanting war because it is simpler than doubt.

nodes.label: Shrine Warning
text: Calia offers watered wine and tells you the cypress roots 🌿 under Selucor were planted before empire claimed the hill.
"Old bargains fail noisily," she says. "Listen for what the city repeats."

nodes.label: Morning Work
text: Dawn comes silver and wind-cold over the sea, and the court begins moving again before grief has finished dressing.
You can spend the morning at the archive, the barracks yard, or the harbor customs hall.

nodes.label: Scholar Table
text: Two archivists argue over dates while pretending not to fear the broken chest beside them.
A copied inventory reveals that one marginal note about witness seals was removed years before the final leaves vanished.

nodes.label: Barracks Yard
text: In the barracks yard, grooms tighten girths while officers speak too softly whenever the word Kardesh surfaces.
Soren lets you watch a dispatch board crowded with fresh pins along the river roads.

nodes.label: Customs Hall
text: Customs scribes tally wool, salt fish, wax, and barley beneath cracked frescoes of imperial abundance.
Danira points out that missing grain always seems to vanish just before a council session about border security.

nodes.label: Lost Courier
text: A courier meant for the council arrives breathless, missing one satchel and carrying the wrong seal in the other.
The confusion can lead you to forged wax, the prince's falcon loft, a river rider at the gate, or back into the archive where the mistake began.

nodes.label: Wrong Seal
text: The courier's spare packet carries the chancellor's household seal pressed in cheap wax and trimmed too cleanly at the edge.
Forgers often copy images; they rarely copy pressure.

nodes.label: Falcon Ribbon
text: In the loft above the schoolroom, the prince's white falcon wears a fresh ribbon stamped with the bridge-fort mark.
Alexen insists he never tied it there and looks more intrigued than afraid.

nodes.label: River Rider
text: At the gate, a river rider from the west asks for Soren and carries mud from roads that should be dry this season.
He says someone reopened an old causeway near the ruined bridge fort.

nodes.label: Follow Clue
text: The morning finally offers something solid enough to chase.
You can study the forged wax, question the river rider, or place the clue in Tamar's hands and see what the envoy notices.

nodes.label: Wax Trace
text: Under lamp heat, the wax releases traces of fennel oil 🕯️ used in one palace office to keep packets from sticking in summer.
The scent points toward Chancellor Marek Danos more cleanly than any witness would dare.

nodes.label: Fort Name
text: The rider names the ruined bridge fort of Valdaran, once the place where Orsanna and Kardesh exchanged foster sons under the covenant.
Few men at court still remember that part aloud.

nodes.label: Tamar Gloss
text: Tamar studies the ribbon and quietly translates its stitched proverb: "Bridges rot first in secret."
The envoy says it is an old Kardeshi warning against councils that smile too much.

nodes.label: Midday Route
text: Midday draws you in three directions at once: maps, princes, and locked rooms.
You can examine bridge records, dine with Alexen, or search the clerk quarters tied to Marek's office.

nodes.label: Bridge Maps
text: The survey room shows old ferries, toll houses, and two bridges erased from the modern military charts.
Someone has been simplifying the border on paper for years.

nodes.label: Prince Meal
text: Alexen picks at flatbread and olives while asking why adults always call fear by larger names like duty or honor.
When you mention the covenant, he says he has dreamed of a bridge under cypresses three nights in a row.

nodes.label: Clerk Rooms
text: In the clerk quarters you find scraped wax, a cracked tally board, and one hidden key wrapped in ordinary linen.
The room is too careful, which is another form of confession.

nodes.label: Procession Jolt
text: A mourning procession surges through the inner court with drums, incense, and armed ushers clearing space by force. 🥁
You might be knocked toward the market fire, the soldiers' chapel, a fresco alcove, or back into the prince's entourage.

nodes.label: Market Sparks
text: In the lower market, a brazier has overturned and traders are shouting over scorched baskets and spilled grain.
Danira sees sabotage in the timing even if the damage itself is small.

nodes.label: Chapel Smoke
text: The soldiers' chapel is thick with tallow smoke and muttered vows from men who would rather face arrows than uncertainty.
A votive board lists the names of riders lost on roads supposedly held by Orsanna.

nodes.label: Alcove Fresco
text: In a side alcove, soot-darkened frescoes show founders exchanging children beside a bridge instead of swords beside a throne.
Someone later painted imperial banners over the children and failed to hide their outlines.

nodes.label: Answer Unrest
text: Every rumor in Selucor now points toward a different culprit and a different remedy.
You can steady the merchants, back the riders publicly, or follow a hooded monk slipping toward the crypt stairs.

nodes.label: Calm Traders
text: You help Danira sort witnesses from opportunists until the shouting loses some of its hunger.
In thanks, she tells you which grain firms grow rich whenever military escorts become mandatory.

nodes.label: Back Riders
text: With Soren at your shoulder, you speak for the exhausted frontier riders instead of letting the court call them reckless provincials.
The barracks will remember that kindness if things turn hard.

nodes.label: Crypt Stairs
text: The hooded monk leads you beneath the chapel and vanishes, leaving only damp steps, lamp soot, and a carved cypress at the landing.
The lower crypt feels older than the empire above it.

nodes.label: Storm Break
text: A sudden sea storm ⛈️ slams into the hill and turns every corridor, stair, and quay into a choice made under pressure.
You may be trapped in the flooded crypt, delayed at council, driven to the harbor for shelter, or pushed back among the traders again.

nodes.label: Flooded Crypt
text: Water sheets through the lower crypt and reveals a mosaic floor beneath centuries of limewash.
The image shows two rulers kneeling before a bridge while a priestess holds a cypress branch between them.

nodes.label: Delayed Council
text: Council stalls while servants bolt shutters and chase papers across the marble floor.
In the confusion, you hear Marek press for emergency toll powers that would enrich his allies by week's end.

nodes.label: Harbor Shelter
text: Driven to the harbor arcade, you find Tamar watching the storm as if weather were another negotiator at court.
The envoy says broken rituals kill peace more reliably than open hatred.

nodes.label: Read Signs
text: Once the rain passes, you are left with symbols, gossip, and hard reports that do not quite agree.
You can trust the omen of the mosaic, the logic of council, or the evidence from the frontier riders.

nodes.label: Omen Weight
text: The flooded mosaic convinces you the covenant was always more ceremonial and more sacred than the court admits.
What was hidden may matter because it changed who has the right to speak during peace.

nodes.label: Council Logic
text: Council evidence points cleanly toward domestic profiteers using the border to force new taxes and military contracts.
It is persuasive, though perhaps too clean to be the whole truth.

nodes.label: Scout Weight
text: Frontier reports still matter most to you: roads cut, ferries burned, shepherd camps emptied just far enough from the forts to avoid pitched war.
Someone is shaping fear with professional care.

nodes.label: Ride Choice
text: The next clue lies somewhere beyond easy chambers and polished floors.
You can ride with Soren to the north gate, remain at court to watch Marek, or cross by boat to the island shrine.

nodes.label: North Gate
text: You ride out with Soren through a gate lined by petitioners, widows, and mule carts waiting for escort orders.
Beyond the walls, the empire looks poorer and more honest.

nodes.label: Palace Hold
text: You stay within the palace maze and watch Marek's servants move packets between offices that should have no reason to speak.
Secrecy at court is often only speed dressed in silk.

nodes.label: Shrine Boat
text: A narrow boat carries you to the island shrine where votive ribbons snap in the wind and salt gathers on old stone saints.
Calia's younger acolyte says the prince's mother used to pray here before public ceremonies.

nodes.label: Horse Scatter
text: A pack mule rears at a drumbeat and sets horses, porters, and riders lunging in four directions at once.
You may end up at a watchtower, an orchard camp, the stable chapel, or thrown back toward the palace after all.

nodes.label: Tower Smoke
text: From the watchtower, you see three thin smokes along the western road where no villages stand close enough to justify them.
Someone is signaling with frontier discipline inside imperial territory.

nodes.label: Orchard Camp
text: In an abandoned orchard camp, refugees from the river road share watered wine and a map scratched in ash on a plank.
They describe raiders who knew exactly which ferries carried grain and which carried children.

nodes.label: Stable Chapel
text: The tiny chapel beside the stables shelters grooms, tack, and one priest who remembers too much.
He says the covenant once required witnesses from shrine, court, and frontier together, never one alone.

nodes.label: Third Inquiry
text: The roads now speak in fragments, and each fragment makes the others heavier.
You can question the refugees, read the smoke signals, or search the abandoned saddlebags left near the chapel.

nodes.label: Refugee Story
text: One elderly boatman insists the raiders spared a shrine wagon but seized tax books before taking grain.
That choice makes no sense unless someone needed records altered, not supplies stolen.

nodes.label: Signal Pattern
text: The smoke pattern matches old Kardeshi field marks for "delay," yet Tamar swears no envoy riders were sent west.
It feels like imitation meant to stain the wrong people.

nodes.label: False Dispatch
text: Inside the abandoned bags lie spare seals, dried figs, and a dispatch naming Marek's cousins as emergency grain contractors.
At last the border trouble has a ledger attached to it.

nodes.label: Return Way
text: With the light slipping toward evening, you need to bring what you know back into Selucor without losing it to chance.
You can take the ferry, the ridge road, or the orchard path below the walls.

nodes.label: Ferry Wake
text: The ferry rocks under carts, soldiers, and frightened hens while the city hill darkens ahead of you.
A ferryman mutters that the river has carried too many sealed boxes this week for a season of mourning.

nodes.label: Ridge Road
text: The ridge road gives you a full view of Selucor, all bronze domes above the black harbor like something too beautiful to trust.
From here, the palace seems built directly on its own forgetting.

nodes.label: Orchard Path
text: The orchard path skirts refugee fires and old walls where children play at coronations with sticks for scepters.
One girl declares that bridges choose kings better than crowns do.

nodes.label: River Fog
text: Sea fog folds into the river mouth and erases distances, bells, and half the lower harbor in one patient breath.
You may land at the shrine quay, the harbor steps, the broken aqueduct, or circle back toward the ferry landing again.

nodes.label: Shrine Quay
text: The fog opens briefly on the shrine quay where votive lamps float like low stars against the stone steps.
Calia is there already, as though she expected the river to choose for you.

nodes.label: Harbor Steps
text: You come in by the harbor steps where Danira's men are arguing over missing manifests and three sacks of wax tablets.
The whole quay feels one rumor away from violence.

nodes.label: Broken Aqueduct
text: The fog lifts beside a broken aqueduct arch scrawled with recent chalk marks and an old bridge sigil.
Someone has been using forgotten imperial masonry as a meeting place.

nodes.label: Seek Counsel
text: By now you know too much to keep moving alone without choosing whose judgment matters most.
You can ask Calia, Danira, or Iria to help interpret what the city is really doing.

nodes.label: Calia Reed
text: Calia says covenants die first in ritual and only later in law. "If witnesses are broken apart," she warns, "power forgets its limits."
The shrine wants reunion more than punishment.

nodes.label: Danira Grain
text: Danira spreads invoices across a tavern table and shows you exactly who grew rich from convoy panic and bridge closures.
Marek's allies have been selling fear by the wagon.

nodes.label: Iria Grief
text: Alone at last, Iria admits her brother let Marek grow powerful because order was easier to buy than justice.
Her voice makes clear she does not intend the same bargain.

nodes.label: Hidden Page
text: One proof still eludes you: the missing witness line that could turn suspicion into certainty.
You can search the annex, inspect the aqueduct marks, or compare your dispatches against Tamar's copies.

nodes.label: Annex Dust
text: In a locked annex drawer you find a copyist's scrap naming three witness seats: crown, cypress, and saddle.
The final line is torn away, but the structure of the rite is suddenly clear.

nodes.label: Aqueduct Marks
text: The chalk marks at the aqueduct prove to be meeting signs used by state couriers before the civil wars.
Marek has been using the empire's oldest routes to hide the newest crimes.

nodes.label: Paired Copies
text: Tamar's archive copy keeps a marginal note Orsanna omitted: the covenant required the prince to hear the pledge, not merely benefit from it.
That single phrase could shift the ceremony from spectacle to accountability.

nodes.label: Feast Shuffle
text: The mourning feast becomes a small war of seating charts, precedence, and quiet sabotage as servants change place cards at the last breath.
You may end up beside Marek, beside Tamar, beside the prince, or slipping out to seek counsel once more.

nodes.label: Chancellor Seat
text: Marek dines with impeccable restraint, speaking of duty while his rings catch every candle in the room.
He watches you with the ease of a man who believes evidence can still be priced.

nodes.label: Envoy Seat
text: Tamar uses the feast to speak of horses, salt, and weather while saying very little about peace itself.
Only once does the envoy murmur that Kardesh remembers every foster child not returned.

nodes.label: Prince Seat
text: Alexen sits too straight in mourning black and asks whether a ruler may obey truth even when his council hates it.
He is young enough to ask the question honestly and old enough to understand the answer may hurt.

nodes.label: Table Answer
text: The feast gives you one chance to shift the balance without drawing open steel.
You can flatter Marek into carelessness, bait him into revealing too much, or keep the pressure off Alexen.

nodes.label: Silver Praise
text: You praise Marek's efficiency until vanity loosens his caution.
He boasts that empires are held by men who keep roads profitable, not by children reciting dead promises.

nodes.label: Sharp Bait
text: You ask whether the missing leaves trouble him, and his fork pauses one beat too long.
The smallest hesitation can become a door if one is patient enough.

nodes.label: Quiet Shield
text: You turn the conversation away from Alexen and let the prince breathe for a few precious minutes.
Iria notices, and so does Tamar, though each values it for different reasons.

nodes.label: After Feast
text: Once the plates clear, Selucor grows quieter and more dangerous.
You can trail the suspicious clerk, lift the hidden key into safer hands, or tell Soren what the ledgers now prove.

nodes.label: Shadow Clerk
text: The clerk leaves by servant passages, checks twice for pursuit, and heads toward the old tower rather than Marek's office.
Guilt, it seems, prefers lonely architecture.

nodes.label: Hidden Key
text: You palm the wrapped key from the clerk room before dawn staff can tidy the evidence into oblivion.
It is heavy bronze, old enough to belong to the first palace rather than the current one.

nodes.label: Tell Soren
text: Soren listens without interruption while sharpening a knife that no ceremony will see.
When you finish, he says peace may still be possible, but only if truth arrives before panic does.

nodes.label: Midnight Bells
text: At midnight, shrine bells strike out of rhythm with the palace clock and send guards, servants, and plotters colliding in the dark.
The disruption may throw you into patrol lines, draw you below to the shrine, pull you toward the tower shadow, or force you back into your earlier choice.

nodes.label: Corridor Watch
text: Patrols thicken in the upper corridors, and one nervous guard admits he was ordered to watch the tower stairs, not the prince.
That inversion tells you exactly where fear sits tonight.

nodes.label: Shrine Call
text: In the under-hill shrine, Calia says the bells answered movement above the roots, not the other way around.
She tells you to choose whether truth should be spoken, hidden, or handed to the child who must bear it.

nodes.label: Tower Shadow
text: At the old tower, the clerk disappears through a bronze door half-hidden behind scaffolding and prayer banners.
The key in your sleeve seems suddenly much less hypothetical.

nodes.label: Tower Find
text: Inside the tower are dust, rat droppings, a reading stand, and the hush of a place used by people who believed themselves invisible.
You can open the bronze chest, read the prayer book on the stand, or wake Alexen and force innocence into the room.

nodes.label: Bronze Chest
text: The chest contains the missing leaves, three forged convoy orders, and a witness list with Marek's cipher in the margin.
At last, theft and profit share the same box.

nodes.label: Prayer Book
text: The book is a Book of Hours once owned by Alexen's mother, filled with notes on river vows and foster law.
One line insists that a prince must hear the covenant before he can rightfully receive the crown.

nodes.label: Waking Alexen
text: Alexen comes to the tower without complaint and reads the first visible line of the witness text with unnerving calm. 📜
"So they were all supposed to stand together," he says. "No wonder someone separated them."

nodes.label: Use Tablet
text: Proof is now in your hands, but proof is never the same as wisdom.
You can name the clerk immediately, hide the tablet until ceremony, or bring everything to Iria before dawn.

nodes.label: Name Clerk
text: You drag the clerk into lamplight and crack the story open just enough to hear Marek's name hiss through frightened teeth.
It is satisfying, but public noise carries risks of its own.

nodes.label: Hide Tablet
text: You wrap the leaves in plain cloth and conceal them where no elegant search would think to look.
Sometimes survival belongs to the unceremonious.

nodes.label: Bring Iria
text: Iria reads the missing text with her face gone still as carved ivory.
When she looks up, grief and fury have settled into something colder and more useful.

nodes.label: Courtyard Panic
text: Before dawn fully breaks, a bolting mare, screaming servants, and clashing guard orders throw the lower courtyard into chaos.
You may be dragged toward the stables, into the servant crush, up the guard stair, or forced to hide the tablet all over again.

nodes.label: Bolting Mare
text: The mare smashes a cart wheel and nearly kills a groom before Soren's men bring her down with blankets and patience.
In the wreckage you find one more crate of forged convoy seals.

nodes.label: Servant Crush
text: In the servant crush, two kitchen boys swear they carried midnight trays to the tower for Marek's household all month.
Conspiracies, like courts, rely on underpaid people remembering everything.

nodes.label: Guard Stair
text: The guard stair gives you a clean path to the upper galleries where ceremony banners already hang over the bridge court.
Selucor is preparing to celebrate before deciding whether it deserves to.

nodes.label: Final Prep
text: The last day before crowning pulls every faction toward its chosen ground.
You can ride for the bridge fort, question the old commander who once kept foster records, or stay in Selucor for palace preparations.

nodes.label: Bridge Fort
text: At ruined Valdaran, wind moves through empty arches where sworn children once crossed between realms under escort.
The place feels less abandoned than waiting.

nodes.label: Old Commander
text: The retired commander keeps goats now, but his memory for protocol has not softened.
He confirms that no coronation under the covenant is lawful unless shrine, saddle, and crown all witness it together.

nodes.label: Palace Weave
text: Staying in Selucor lets you watch ceremony workers lace banners over the bridge court while Marek's allies push for extra guards and closed doors.
The stage is being built for either peace or a very elegant theft of it.

nodes.label: Core Truth
text: By now the structure of the betrayal is clear, but its most useful edge still depends on what you emphasize.
You can read the covenant whole, follow the silver behind the raids, or ask Alexen what kind of reign he wants.

nodes.label: Full Covenant
text: The restored text binds Orsanna and Kardesh not only to peace but to shared toll rights, foster exchange, and public witness before the prince.
Marek stole more than leaves; he stole the ceremony's meaning.

nodes.label: Silver Trail
text: Danira's ledgers and the forged convoy orders prove Marek's cousins turned every raid rumor into contracts, levies, and escort fees.
War was becoming an investment portfolio.

nodes.label: Prince Resolve
text: Alexen listens longer than most adults and says he would rather be embarrassed by truth than protected by a lie he must inherit.
The sentence is simple enough to shame half the court.

nodes.label: Market Surge
text: On the morning of the ceremony, the lower market erupts with rumor: Kardesh plots treachery, the prince is cursed, the bridges are closed.
The surge can draw you into a harbor speech, the shrine lots, a forced return to palace preparations, or back toward the palace weave again.

nodes.label: Harbor Cry
text: At the harbor rail, Danira shouts down panic by reading prices aloud and naming the men who benefit if ships stop moving.
Sometimes commerce is the only language a frightened crowd still trusts.

nodes.label: Shrine Lots
text: At the shrine, Calia casts cypress lots into a bronze bowl and tells you the old pact can still be renewed if spoken by the right mouths together.
She means you are no longer merely an observer.

nodes.label: Palace Return
text: Back at the bridge court, Iria stands in mourning white while Soren stations riders with visible reluctance and visible skill.
Marek smiles the smile of a man who thinks ceremonies belong to whoever controls the doors.

nodes.label: Final Side
text: When the bells begin, you must decide which center of power to strengthen before truth enters the open air.
You can stand with Iria, with Soren, or with Calia and the old form of the oath.

nodes.label: Regent Path
text: You take your place near Iria and the prince, where speech can still alter the shape of the ceremony before steel does.
It is the most dangerous kind of loyalty because everyone can see it.

nodes.label: Captain Path
text: You move beside Soren and the frontier riders, where peace must survive suspicion long enough to be declared.
One bad command will turn the bridge court into a battlefield.

nodes.label: Keeper Stand
text: Calia lifts the cypress branch and waits for your answer while the bells gather under the dome.
You can renew the old oath before all witnesses, or carry the truth away from court before empire swallows it again.

nodes.label: Regent Stand
text: Iria gives you one breath to choose the shape of revelation.
You can read the covenant aloud yourself, or place the leaves in Alexen's hands and let the prince claim truth as his first act.

nodes.label: Captain Stand
text: Soren asks whether the riders should hold the court open for peace or strike first when Marek's men begin to move.
What you answer will decide whether fear serves order or devours it.

nodes.label: Peace Bridges
text: The covenant is read before shrine, saddle, crown, and envoy, and the bridge court falls into the shocked silence that real truth earns. ⚖️
Marek is stripped of office, Alexen is crowned under witness rather than flattery, and Orsanna chooses a hard peace that may finally endure.

nodes.label: Hidden Chronicle
text: You place the leaves in Alexen's hands, and the boy prince speaks the restored oath himself with a steadiness no tutor could invent.
The court learns that memory can govern as surely as force, and you remain to write the first honest chronicle Selucor has seen in years.

nodes.label: Iron Falcon
text: When Marek's faction reaches for blades, Soren's riders move faster and the bridge court becomes a lesson written in steel.
Orsanna survives under an iron peace and a sharpened frontier, but everyone present understands how much beauty was lost to keep the realm intact.

nodes.label: Cypress Oath
text: Under Calia's branch 🌿, Iria, Alexen, Tamar, and Soren stand together where the founders once stood, and the old oath is renewed in the form empire tried to erase.
Power changes shape that morning: less splendid, more bounded, and far harder for men like Marek to steal.

nodes.label: Road Dust
text: You leave Selucor before applause can turn you into another ornament of the court, carrying copied leaves and the names of all who tried to bury them.
Behind you the empire must decide what to do with truth; ahead of you, the roads remain uncertain, honest, and wonderfully free of ceremony.
